correctness.rationale: C follows from the inspected Laface–Ugaglia 2026 Theorem 3 and the explicit integral-character sparse-interval lemma. For any bad positive triple every cyclic gap contains two or more rays, forcing at least nine. The nine primitive rays form a complete smooth fan (all cyclic determinants are one), and the selected triple has character pairings congruent modulo three and of zero sum, so every nontrivial lattice binomial has at least two selected variables in each monomial. This proves squared-ideal containment for all characters. The finite checker corroborates but is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Provides the first possible fan and Picard complexity of needing higher-Rees-multiplicity Cox generators for any smooth toric surface blown up at a torus point, valid uniformly across infinitely many fans including unbounded Hirzebruch parameters. The three-gap obstruction pinpoints the geometric reason and the nine-ray witness makes the bound sharp. It controls a stronger invariant than finite generation and can reduce the necessity of searching for higher-multiplicity generators in explicit calculations.
